editorial:
Imagine being a young guy who thinks he is destined for greatness in the army, but everything that can go wrong actually does. That is exactly what happens to Jürgen. He joins the military in West Germany with big dreams of being a hero, but he is just not cut out for the strict life of a soldier. The vibe here is a total mess in the best way possible. You get to watch him fumble through basic training and clash with the system, which makes for some really funny and awkward moments. It is a lighthearted look at how some people just do not fit into the mold of a rigid military structure.

What really makes this movie work is how it shifts from a military comedy into a weird story about a sanatorium. The acting is goofy and the pacing keeps things moving along without getting boring. While some of the jokes feel a bit old, the sheer randomness of the plot is a huge plus. If you like comedies that poke fun at authority, you should definitely check this one out.
endingExplained: In the end, Jürgen finds that he is much better off away from the army. After his wild ride through the military and the strange sanatorium, the movie wraps up by showing that his attempts to be a soldier were a total failure. He finally accepts that he does not fit in with the rigid rules of the military. He ends up finding a sense of peace by simply being himself instead of trying to be a hero.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school comedies about underdogs.
